title: Deployment Roadmap Lab — Operational Runway & Slide Outline
content:
Purpose:
This lab is a pragmatic, customer-facing workshop to co-create the deployment roadmap (the operational runway) for a mid-sized product team migrating from Redwood Hosted API to a Dedicated deployment. The focus is on scope, risk, metrics, and an actionable 6–12 week cutover plan that the customer engineering and platform teams can execute with Redwood SE and SRE support.

Audience:
- Customer product engineering, platform/infra, and security stakeholders
- Redwood SE lead + solutions architect + SRE liaison

Session length: 3 hours (recommended) — can be split into two 90-minute sessions for busy execs.

Pre-work (sent 3–5 days before):
- Simple intake form (team, SLA targets, current qps and p95 latency, peak hour qps, data residency constraints, audit/retention requirements)
- Ask for a small sample traffic profile (CSV: timestamp, requests, avg prompt tokens, avg response tokens) or provide sample payloads
- Attach relevant network topology / VPC diagram (optional)

Goal / Desired outcomes by end of workshop:
1) Agreed deployment target (Dedicated cluster size and baseline model variant)
2) Cutover risk map and mitigation plan (3 highest risks with owners)
3) 6-week sprint-level roadmap with acceptance criteria for each milestone
4) Clear list of operational runbooks to produce (autoscale policy, failover, rollback, observability playbook)

Agenda (3 hours):
- 0:00–0:10 Welcome & objectives (SE lead) — set expectations, success criteria, confirm pre-work received
- 0:10–0:30 Current state + constraints (Customer 1-pager + metrics) — quick readout from customer; facilitator clarifies unknowns
- 0:30–1:00 Traffic & cost archetype mapping exercise (group) — map traffic profile to recommended bounding configs (batching, cache, quantization)
- 1:00–1:25 Failure modes & risk mapping (group) — draw top failure scenarios, estimate impact and likelihood, assign mitigations
- 1:25–1:35 Break
- 1:35–2:05 Cutover runway design (SE-led) — recommended Dedicated sizing, canary strategy, fallback model variants, network/cert steps
- 2:05–2:40 Sprint roadmap & milestones (group breakout) — create sprint cards with owners and acceptance criteria (3 sprints recommended)
- 2:40–2:55 Operational playbook and observability checklist (SRE/SE) — what to instrument, alert thresholds, dashboards to create
- 2:55–3:00 Next steps, owners, and immediate actions

Facilitator notes & scripts (practical tips):
- Before workshop: triage pre-work — if traffic profile missing, run quick synthetic profile using sample prompts and assume 30% daily peak variance.
- Opening: call out the three measurable outcomes you must leave with (target config, top 3 risks, sprint plan). Keep these visible on a shared board.
- On the traffic mapping exercise: show two example archetypes (burst/interactive chat vs streaming multi-turn) and their effect on batching and KV cache. Use real numbers where possible (e.g., 200 qps peak, avg 60 tokens in request, 150 tokens in response).
- Risk mapping prompts: "What happens if the model becomes token-expensive during black friday?" "What network ACL or cert change could block callouts?"
- When proposing Dedicated sizing, present a conservative baseline and an optimistic baseline (e.g., 2x reserved vs 1x reserved) and the expected cost delta and latency SLA impact.
- Keep decisions timeboxed — use 5/2/1 minute queues for quick votes on low-impact items.

Slide outline (speaker + slide notes):
1) Title + objectives (30s) — list the 3 outcomes, team introductions
2) Customer snapshot (1 slide) — key metrics, critical constraints (security, latency, capacity)
3) Traffic archetypes & sample payloads (1 slide) — visual heatmap of peak vs baseline, token distribution
4) Configuration levers (1 slide) — batching, prefix/KV caching, quantization, sequence truncation, model variant mapping
5) Cost vs latency decision matrix (2 slides) — example tradeoffs and recommended knobs for each archetype
6) Failure modes & risk map (1 slide) — top 5 risks and mitigations with owners
7) Dedicated cluster recommendation (1 slide) — instance types, baseline concurrency, autoscale thresholds, expected throughput
8) Canary & rollback strategy (1 slide) — traffic split plan, monitoring guardrails, automated fallback triggers
9) 6-week sprint-level runway (1 slide) — milestone cards and owners
10) Observability & runbooks (1 slide) — required dashboards, metric thresholds, alert runbook links
11) Acceptance criteria + next steps (1 slide) — who does what by when, follow-up meeting cadence

Breakout templates (use Miro / Jamboard / Google Slides):
- Sprint card template: title; owner; IAC/infra work required; test plan; acceptance criteria; rollout window
- Risk card template: risk description; impact (1–5); likelihood (1–5); mitigation action; owner; confidence level
- Metric card: metric name; collection frequency; dashboard location; alert threshold; who responds

Example facilitator script snippets (copy/paste):
- "We have 20 minutes for traffic mapping: sketch the traffic profile you expect in an average hour and a peak hour. Don't worry about exact numbers — we'll translate later."
- "For the canary strategy, assume we start at 1% of traffic, observe 30 minutes of user-facing latency and error metrics, then 10x increase cadence if stable."
- "If we see token costs exceed forecasts by 25% in production, the rollback plan is to switch to a lower-context model variant and enable aggressive prefix caching — who on your team owns that toggle?"

Artifacts to deliver after the workshop (within 3 business days):
- Draft runway slide deck (editable) capturing decisions and recommended config
- Sprint backlog exported as a CSV (milestone, owner, due date, acceptance criteria)
- Risk register (top 10) with mitigations and owners
- Draft runbooks list and suggested dashboard templates

Acceptance criteria for 'ready for Dedicated cutover' (example checklist):
- Benchmarked Dedicated cluster with expected throughput >= 1.1x peak traffic
- Canary automation scripts in place (traffic shaping + automated fallback)
- Network peers and certs validated (no outstanding firewall rules)
- Observability: p95 latency, error rate, token cost per request instrumented and dashboarded
- Rollback plan documented and rehearsed once in staging

Common pitfalls & how to avoid them:
- Pitfall: diving too deep into infra sizing before understanding traffic shape — avoid by running the mapping exercise first.
- Pitfall: forgetting downstream consumers (webhooks, downstream services) — add a check box to the intake form.
- Pitfall: underestimating rollback complexity — capture rollback steps as discrete tickets during the workshop.

Follow-up cadence recommendation:
- Weekly 30m sync for first 6 weeks after workshop (owners updates, SRE escalation)
- Two-week engineering review sync aligned to sprint boundaries

Notes to SE (internal):
- Bring a small library of pre-computed throughput numbers for common instance types (e.g., A100, H100, and mainstream T4-like equivalence) to accelerate recommendations.
- Have canned Dashboard JSONs and PromQL queries ready to drop in customer's monitoring system.
- Prepare a templated canary playbook that can be customized during the session.

Appendix: quick intake form fields to send to customer (copy/paste):
- Team name and primary contacts (name, email, pager)
- Target SLA (p95 latency and error budget)
- Peak qps and average qps (or sample CSV)
- Expected request/response token sizes (avg and 95th)
- Data residency / compliance constraints
- Existing monitoring stack and dashboard access
- Deployment window constraints (maintenance windows)

End of document.
